en.title: Ubisoft Milan Pitched a Ganondorf-Led Zelda Game to Nintendo
en.summary: A fascinating 'what if' in gaming history has surfaced: Ubisoft Milan reportedly developed a prototype for a Legend of Zelda spin-off starring Ganondorf. The ambitious project, internally codenamed 'Goliath,' ultimately didn't make it to Nintendo's approval.
en.body:
In a twist that has gamers worldwide speculating, reports have emerged detailing an ambitious project that could have dramatically reshaped the Legend of Zelda series. Ubisoft Milan, the acclaimed studio behind the beloved **Mario + Rabbids** games, reportedly pitched a spin-off title to Nintendo that would have placed the franchise's ultimate antagonist, **Ganondorf**, in the starring role. The game, internally codenamed **Goliath**, was envisioned as a departure from the traditional Link-centric adventures, exploring a new universe with an entirely original protagonist before Nintendo's surprising pivot.

According to insider information, Nintendo itself requested that the protagonist be changed to **Ganondorf** during the early concept phase. This dramatic shift would have marked the first time the Gerudo King was the central playable character in any Zelda title, a concept that, on paper, sounds like a bold and potentially groundbreaking addition to the series. Former Ubisoft developer Gian Marco Zanna even described the project with considerable enthusiasm, calling it a “new big bang in the video game universe.” However, despite the studio's efforts to develop a prototype by a late 2023 deadline, Nintendo reportedly rejected the proposal, leading to the project's cancellation.

## The "Goliath" Concept

The **Goliath** project was apparently conceived shortly after the successful launch of **Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope**, with Ubisoft Milan eager to tackle another major IP. While details on the original protagonist remain scarce, the shift to **Ganondorf** suggests a game that would have delved deep into the lore and motivations of the King of Evil. Imagine a game exploring his rise to power, his struggles, or perhaps even a redemption arc – possibilities that have long been a source of fan fascination. The sheer scale and ambition of what Ubisoft Milan hoped to achieve with **Goliath** seem to have been immense, aiming to create something truly distinct within the vast Zelda universe.

## A Missed Opportunity for Fans?

The news has sparked considerable discussion among fans, many of whom are lamenting the loss of what could have been a truly unique gaming experience. The idea of stepping into **Ganondorf**'s boots, exploring his perspective, and experiencing the world of Hyrule (or a new setting) through his eyes is incredibly compelling. It represents a significant "what if" in gaming history, a project that could have offered a fresh, darker, and more character-driven narrative than many Zelda titles. The fact that the project reportedly involved years of work before being shelved makes the cancellation all the more poignant for those who appreciate bold creative risks.

## What's Next

While neither Nintendo nor Ubisoft has officially commented on the **Goliath** project, the reports suggest that Ubisoft Milan has moved on to other endeavors. Fans will undoubtedly keep an eye on future announcements from the studio, hoping that elements of this ambitious **Ganondorf** game might one day resurface, perhaps in a different form or on future Nintendo hardware.

content_raw: Ubisoft Milan reportedly pitched a Zelda game to Nintendo that would have taken place in a new universe with a totally different protagonist, but the plan fell through, leading to one of the biggest what-ifs in gaming history. Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson says the project was internally titled Goliath, so as to appropriately echo the size and scale of what Ubisoft Milan hoped to achieve with the game. It was an ambitious plan, and one that former Ubisoft developer Gian Marco Zanna described as a “new big bang in the video game universe.” This description, while dramatic, is accurate; Ubisoft Milan’s Zelda game would have been drastically different from anything we’ve seen from the series thus far. Rather than following Link’s adventures in the wilds of Hyrule, it would have been a spin-off title in the broader Zelda universe featuring a brand-new, “never-before-seen character.” However, during its early concept phase, Nintendo reportedly asked that this protagonist be changed to the franchise’s ultimate big bad: Ganondorf. This would have been the first time Ganondorf was the central, playable character in a Zelda game, and on paper, it sounds like a fantastic idea… but unfortunately, it didn’t end up coming to fruition. Sources told Henderson that Ubisoft Milan was given a deadline of late 2023 to come up with a prototype for this Ganondorf game, but Nintendo reportedly rejected their proposal when the time came, for reasons that have not been made clear. Ubisoft Milan was behind the highly-lauded Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, which IGN scored a sparkling nine out of 10 . The studio reportedly began ideation for Goliath shortly after its release, clearly riding the high of its successful launch. It’s almost painful to imagine the game we could’ve had; perhaps it was a Ganon origin story? Given that it was a spin-off and not a sequel or prequel, it’s unclear what, exactly, Ganon would be doing in this game. And what about Ubisoft Milan’s first intended protagonist for the project? We have so many questions, and it’s likely that none of them will ever get answered. Ubisoft did not respond to Henderson’s requests for comment, but he did note that it had internally acknowledged a journalist requesting information about Goliath beforehand. Among the oodles of canceled, top-secret games over the years, this one definitely makes us go down the ‘what if’ rabbit hole. It’s almost as tantalizing as the canceled Disney Smash Bros.-style game , which former concept artist Ken Christiansen shared artwork for on his personal online portfolio, showing characters like Captain Hook, the Sheriff of Nottingham, the Queen of Hearts, John Silver, and others facing off in 2v2 battles.
